为我生成一段时长 1分15 秒的电影感流行 MV 视频提示词。

一位女性歌手在月白窗边与晚风归途交错的梦境空间里对着镜头唱歌，口型与歌词同步。开场是深夜卧室窗边的一束月白，纱帘被风慢慢吹起，她赤脚坐在窗台闭眼轻唱，镜头从她指尖的月光缓慢推近嘴唇和麦克风；随后硬切到安静卧室，她把心事折成纸鹤放进枕边，纸鹤与纸船在微光中轻轻悬浮，她边走边唱，手持镜头轻微晃动，夜色像被风吹得很轻；紧接着闪白切到暖黄床头灯下的录音角落，她戴着耳机侧脸对麦克风，手指轻轻打节拍，镜头从手部特写推到脸部，呼吸慢慢靠近；音乐进入副歌时快速跳切到雨后老巷与归家路灯，她仰头高唱“月光晚安”，镜头环绕旋转，路灯频闪，远处行人只剩剪影，晚风陪她走回家；再切到玻璃橱窗和水洼倒影的镜面空间，多个反射中的她同时歌唱，慢动作画面流动，冷蓝月光与暖橙路灯交错；最后黑场后回到窗边她的面部大特写，她直视镜头唱完“我在梦里等你啊”，灯光收暗，只剩轮廓光，镜头慢慢拉远并定格在纱帘、纸鹤和空中的月白。整体节奏卡音乐节拍，硬切、闪白、频闪、跳切交替出现，浅景深，胶片颗粒，逆光轮廓，2.39:1，24fps，电影级质感，时尚大片氛围。

- 提示词要点：不写 `<Audio 1>` 标签；在 `subject_definitions` / `summary` / `detailed_description` 三处显式声明 "口型与驱动音频逐音节同步"，每个 Shot 说话时再补充具体的嘴部开合、下颌运动细节。

**subject_definitions:**
`<Subject 1>` is the young East Asian female singer shown in `<Picture 1>`, with dark hair pulled into a low ponytail, natural dewy makeup and warm terracotta lips, wearing a champagne ivory silk satin slip dress with thin spaghetti straps and a draped cowl neckline, and a thin silver necklace with a textured heart-shaped pendant. Her lip movements are synchronized syllable-by-syllable with the driving audio.

**summary:**
[reference generation + audio reuse] The target video is a 75-second cinematic pop music video in which `<Subject 1>` performs the song across a series of dreamlike spaces—a moonlit bedroom window, a quiet bedroom with floating origami, a warm recording corner, a post-rain old alley under flickering streetlights, and a glass-and-puddle mirror world—culminating in a return to the window close-up. Her lip movements are synchronized syllable-by-syllable with the driving audio throughout. The reference image defines her facial features, hairstyle, dress, and necklace, while the driving audio supplies the complete vocal performance and instrumental arrangement.

**retention_analysis:**
`<Subject 1>` (appears in all shots): fully_preserved — the singer's facial features, dark low ponytail, champagne silk slip dress, and silver heart pendant necklace remain consistent across every environment and lighting change.

**detailed_description:**
The target video is a cinematic pop music video in 2.39:1 widescreen at 24fps, with shallow depth of field, fine film grain, backlit rim lighting, and alternating hard cuts, flash-white transitions, brief light strobing, and jump cuts synced to the music beat. The color palette shifts between cool moonlit blue and warm tungsten orange. Throughout every shot, `<Subject 1>`'s lip movements are synchronized syllable-by-syllable with the driving audio.

[Shot 1] The scene opens in a deep-night bedroom. A shaft of pale moon-white light falls across a large window where sheer white curtains drift inward in a soft breeze. `<Subject 1>` sits barefoot on the windowsill in her champagne silk slip dress, eyes gently closed, singing into a small condenser microphone on a stand. The camera begins on a close-up of her fingertips resting on the moonlit sill, then slowly pushes in at a steady speed along her arm up to her lips and the microphone. Her lips part softly on each incoming syllable, jaw relaxed and slightly dropped, breath carrying the opening phrase. She sings, <d>[Chinese] 窗边有一点月白，落在你的指尖上，风从纱帘慢慢过，把夜色吹得很轻。</d> Her mouth opens wider on the sustained "月白" and closes softly on "轻", the lower jaw tracing small relaxed arcs with each word.

[Shot 2] At 00:12.000, a hard cut lands on a wider view of the same quiet bedroom, now dimmer. `<Subject 1>` stands beside a made bed, folding a sheet of pale paper into an origami crane, her lips moving continuously as she sings. She places the finished crane on the pillow; several paper cranes and folded paper boats hover weightlessly in the faint air around her, catching tiny points of light. She begins walking slowly across the room while singing; the camera follows with a handheld shot that shakes slightly, as if the night air itself is tremulous. She sings, <d>[Chinese] 我把心事折成纸，放进安静的梦里，你不用说太多话，我也懂你的疲惫。</d> Her lips purse slightly on the folded consonants of "折成纸", the jaw making small downward movements on each phrase ending, and her mouth stays half-open as she inhales softly between lines.

[Shot 3] At 00:24.000, a flash-white cut bleeds into a warm-lit recording corner. A single amber bedside lamp glows from the left, pooling warm yellow light on a small desk. `<Subject 1>` wears over-ear headphones, shown in profile facing a professional microphone. Her right-hand fingers tap a gentle rhythmic pattern on the desk surface in time with the beat. The camera starts on a close-up of her tapping fingers, then pushes in slowly along her arm and shoulder toward her face as her breath comes closer to the mic. She sings in a softer, more intimate register, <d>[Chinese] 慢一点，让呼吸靠近，别怕黑，我在这里。</d> On "慢一点" her lips stretch into a soft rounded shape and the jaw drops gently; on "别怕黑" the mouth opens wider with a slight forward push of the jaw; on "我在这里" her lips form a small closed smile before parting for the final sustained vowel.

[Shot 4] At 00:34.000, quick jump cuts trigger as the music enters the chorus. The scene shifts to a post-rain old alley glistening under amber homecoming streetlights. `<Subject 1>` tilts her head back and looks upward, singing with open vocal projection. The camera circles around her in an arc shot at moderate speed while the streetlights behind her flicker in short strobing pulses. Distant pedestrians appear only as dark blurred silhouettes at the far end of the wet lane. She sings, <d>[Chinese] 月光晚安，月光晚安，把今天轻轻放下，晚风晚安，晚风晚安，陪你走回家。</d> Her mouth opens wide on the high sustained "月光晚安", jaw dropping emphatically on each "晚安", and her lips form a rounded "wu" shape on "晚风" before relaxing on "陪你走回家".

[Shot 5] At 00:49.000, the shot cuts to a surreal mirror space: a glass storefront window on one side and dark rain-puddled asphalt on the other, multiplying her reflection across dozens of reflective surfaces. `<Subject 1>` stands at the center, and every reflected copy of her sings simultaneously in slow motion. Cold blue moonlight from above and warm orange streetlight from below cross-cut across her face and the glass. The camera drifts laterally at slow speed as ripples spread across the puddles, distorting the reflections. She sings, <d>[Chinese] 月光晚安，月光晚安，闭上眼就不慌张，晚风晚安，晚风晚安。</d> In slow motion, her jaw drops deliberately on each "月光晚安", lips parting and closing with exaggerated smoothness on "闭上眼就不慌张"; every reflected copy matches the exact same lip shape and jaw angle at every syllable.

[Shot 6] At 01:04.000, a brief black screen transitions back to the original moonlit bedroom window. The shot is an extreme close-up of `<Subject 1>`'s face, now fully turned toward the camera, looking directly into the lens. The practical lights have faded to near darkness; only a cool rim light traces the edge of her hair and shoulder. She sings the final line tenderly, <d>[Chinese] 我在梦里等你啊。</d> Her eyes hold steady on the camera, lips shaping each word with deliberate softness—the mouth opens gently on "我在梦里", closes to a small rounded shape on "等你", and opens on the final drawn-out "啊", jaw relaxing as the sound fades. After the final note, the camera slowly pulls out at a very slow speed, widening from her face to reveal the sheer curtains drifting in the moonlight, the hovering paper cranes, and the pale moonbeam hanging suspended in the air. The frame freezes on this final composition as the last light dims.

**overall_soundscape:**
A soft night wind sighs through the bedroom curtains throughout the opening shots. Faint paper rustling accompanies the folding of the origami crane, followed by the almost inaudible whisper of weightless paper objects drifting in the air. Wet footsteps echo softly on the rain-slicked alley pavement in the chorus sequence, with distant muffled traffic and the patter of residual raindrops on glass. Close-mic breath sounds are audible between phrases in the recording-corner shot.

**non_diegetic_music:**
The driving audio track provides the complete cinematic pop ballad arrangement—a sparse piano-led verse with soft ambient pads, building into a fuller chorus with gentle electronic percussion and warm sustained strings, and pulling back to a quiet piano-and-vocal finish for the outro. The arrangement's dynamics and beat drive all visual cuts and camera rhythm.
